note: For electric motors, pumps, compressors, and related fluid-handling equipment, CBP usually finds that origin is conferred by the manufacture of the core functional mechanism, such as the stator and rotor, impeller, rotary group, compressor unit, or heavy-duty machined fluid-end housing, or by extensive local sheet-metal fabrication combined with multi-stage subassembly. Simple mechanical assembly of pre-manufactured motors, impellers, switches, valves, and control boards into a housing, or minor finishing of imported blanks, does not constitute a substantial transformation.

groups.name: Electric motor stator and rotor
operations: Manufacture the motor stator and rotor from laminations and windings
Assemble the motor with capacitors, fan, shaft, mounting plate, and seals

precedent.note: CBP found that manufacturing the stator and rotor in the assembly country conferred origin to a vacuum pump (N344081) and that sourcing a complete motor from China kept origin in China for a condensate pump (N347899), whereas sourcing finished motors from China did not determine origin when extensive chassis fabrication and subassembly occurred elsewhere (N347270, N347271, N347272).

groups.name: Impeller, rotary group, and fluid mechanism
operations: Produce the impeller, cylinder block with piston bores, hydraulic pistons, and crankshaft
Cut, spline, and turn the power transmitting driveshaft
Drill balance holes, trim the outside diameter, and bore the inside diameter of the impeller
Construct compressor, evaporator, and condenser cooling subassemblies

precedent.note: CBP held that the origin of pumps, hydraulic motors, and heat pumps is determined by the country producing the impeller (N333514, N347899), the rotary group and housing (N344048), or the majority of the compressor and cooling components (N348913), while minor machining of an imported impeller and shaft in Canada was not enough to change origin (N333514).

groups.name: Housing, chassis, and machined block
operations: Machine, drill cylinders, heat treat, mill, and bore forged steel blocks into a finished fluid-end housing
Stamp, bend, weld, and powder coat steel sheet into chassis panels and mounting plates
Stretch, form, trim, flange, and punch steel coil into compressor outer shell cases
Cast or mold outer housings, bottom plates, shroud covers, and tanks

precedent.note: Full machining and heat treatment of a forged steel block into a fluid-end housing (N351810) or stamping, welding, and powder coating the steel chassis panels alongside subassembly production (N347270, N347271, N347272) conferred origin, whereas rough forging an unfinished block (N351810) or supplying the outer housing and base plate of a vacuum pump (N344081) did not control origin.

groups.name: Control boards, switches, and valves
operations: Manufacture the printed circuit board assembly (PCBA) and main control board
Assemble float switches, micro-switches, thermostats, sensors, and brackets
Press valve inserts into valve bodies and assemble discharge flanges, tees, and O-rings

precedent.note: Sourcing the PCBA or control board from China (N344081, N347270, N347271, N347272) or assembling switches, floats, and valves from imported parts (N347899, N351810) was not enough to confer origin over the country producing the core mechanical or structural assemblies.

groups.name: Final assembly, lubrication, and testing
operations: Install the motor, impeller, rotary group, or valves into the main housing or chassis
Mount the PCBA, switches, sensors, and covers using fasteners, spacers, and seals
Apply grease or lubricating oil, seal the unit, and perform final testing

precedent.note: Final assembly conferred origin when paired with local production of the motor stator and rotor (N344081) or local steel chassis fabrication and key subassembly manufacturing (N347270, N347271, N347272), but merely assembling imported impellers, motors, cooling components, or machined housings did not confer origin (N333514, N347899, N348913, N351810).
